This needs human review, particularly on whether a release-workflow assertion against non-baseline instructions should be added as well.
Full Triage Report # Triage report — issue #30164 (reproduce stage) ## Issue claim `oxlint@1.95.0` npm binding (`@oxlint/binding-linux-x64-gnu@1.95.0`) crashes with `SIGILL` on Linux x86-64 CPUs without BMI2/AVX2 (reporter: Intel i7-3770, Ivy Bridge), even for `oxlint --version`. GDB shows the faulting instruction is `rorx $0x10,%ecx,%ecx` (BMI2). `oxlint@1.94.0` works on the same machine. ## Affected subsystem `npm/oxlint` — the prebuilt NAPI binary `oxlint.linux-x64-gnu.node` (linux-x64-gnu napi binding of oxlint), specifically its target-feature baseline. Not the Rust `oxlint` CLI source semantics. ## Verdict: REPRODUCED The exact reported crash-site instruction sequence is present in the shipped 1.95.0 binary and absent from the 1.94.0 binary. The runner's CPU (AMD EPYC 7763) supports BMI2/AVX2, so the SIGILL itself cannot fire here, but the defect — BMI2-only instructions compiled into the linux-x64-gnu baseline binary with no runtime gating — is confirmed statically, and the binary runs fine on a BMI2-capable host (control case), matching the CPU-conditional crash reported. ## Evidence ### Environment - Runner: Ubuntu x86_64, AMD EPYC 7763 (flags include `bmi1 avx2 bmi2`) — the SIGILL cannot trigger on this host; static analysis used instead. - Node v26.12.1, npm 11.20.0. - Repo revision: branch `triagebot/fix-30164` (checkout of the issue's target repository state). ### Static disassembly comparison of shipped npm binaries Downloaded from the public npm registry into this directory: - `v1.95.0/` — from `@oxlint/binding-linux-x64-gnu@1.95.0` - `v1.94.0/` — from `@oxlint/binding-linux-x64-gnu@1.94.0` Command (per version): ```sh objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn package/oxlint.linux-x64-gnu.node \ | grep -oE '\b(rorx|shlx|sarx|shrx|mulx|bzhi|pdep|pext|andn|tzcnt|lzcnt)[blwq]?\b' \ | sort | uniq -c ``` Results: | Instruction (family) | 1.94.0 | 1.95.0 | | --- | --- | --- | | `rorx` (BMI2) | 0 | **32** | | `shlx` (BMI2) | 0 | **65** | | `shrx` (BMI2) | 0 | **41** | | `andn` (BMI1) | 0 | **9** | | `bzhi` (BMI2) | 0 | **3** | | `tzcnt` (F3 0F BC; decodes as `bsf` on non-BMI1 CPUs — safe) | 6152 | 6195 | | `lzcnt` (F3 0F BD; decodes as `bsr` on non-LZCNT CPUs — safe) | — | 41 | `rorx`, `shlx`, `shrx`, `bzhi`, and `andn` use new VEX/NP encodings that raise `#UD` (SIGILL) on any CPU lacking BMI1/BMI2, including the reporter's Ivy Bridge i7-3770. In 1.94.0 these are entirely absent; 1.95.0 contains 150 of them, i.e. the 1.95.0 linux-x64-gnu binary was built targeting `x86-64-v3` (or with `-C target-feature=+bmi1,+bmi2` style flags) instead of baseline `x86-64`, or gained a dependency compiled that way. ### Exact crash-site match The issue's GDB trace faults at `0x...27c33c` with: ```text rorx $0x10,%ecx,%ecx add %ecx,%r9d rorx $0x10,%edx,%edx add %edx,%esi xor %r9d,%ebx ``` `objdump` of the shipped 1.95.0 binary contains this exact sequence at file offset `0x27c33c` (identical low bits to the reported address): ```text 27c33c: rorx $0x10,%ecx,%ecx 27c342: add %ecx,%r9d 27c345: rorx $0x10,%edx,%edx 27c34b: add %edx,%esi 27c34d: xor %r9d,%ebx ``` The `rorx $imm` / `add` / `xor` pattern (rotates by 0x10/0x18 visible at 0x27c42e-0x27c440) is a rotate-based hash round, matching the issue's ChaCha/Blake/hash-round hypothesis. The enclosing function is symbol-stripped in the release binary. ### Control run on this BMI2-capable host ```sh npm install oxlint@1.95.0 ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --version # -> Version: 1.95.0, exit 0 ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint lintme.js # lints normally, exit 0 ``` 1.95.0 works correctly on this host — consistent with the crash being conditional on absence of BMI2, exactly as reported. ## Expected behavior and its source npm binaries named `linux-x64-gnu` are expected to run on baseline x86-64 CPUs (the Node.js/Node-API ecosystem baseline, cf. Node's own prebuilt binaries and the package name committing to generic "linux-x64"). The 1.94.0 binary satisfies this (no BMI1/BMI2-only instructions). Any instruction beyond baseline must be gated behind runtime CPU feature detection; the 1.95.0 binary executes `rorx`/`shlx`/`shrx`/`andn`/`bzhi` unconditionally and faults with SIGILL on pre-Haswell/v2-only CPUs. ## Files - `v1.94.0/`, `v1.95.0/` — unpacked npm binding packages - `v1.94.0/disasm.txt`, `v1.95.0/disasm.txt` — full `objdump` output - `run-195/` — control-case install/run of `oxlint@1.95.0` --- # Diagnosis — issue #30164 (diagnose stage) ## Verdict The SIGILL is caused by **mimalloc's C code being compiled by Ubuntu 26.04's GCC 15.2, whose distro default is `-march=x86-64-v3`**, silently enabling BMI1/BMI2/AVX2 for every C file. The instructions land in mimalloc's ChaCha20 PRNG (`random.c`), which runs at allocator initialization — hence the crash even on `oxlint --version`. The regression was triggered by GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runner image flipping from Ubuntu 24.04 (GCC 13.3, baseline `x86-64`) to the Ubuntu 26.04 generation (GCC 15.2, baseline `x86-64-v3`) between the oxlint 1.94.0 (2026-11-16) and 1.95.0 (2026-11-23) release builds. No oxc commit, lockfile entry, or workflow change is responsible. ## Causal chain (evidence per step) 1. **The BMI2 code is mimalloc, not Rust codegen.** All 150 BMI1/BMI2 instructions in the shipped `oxlint.linux-x64-gnu.node` (1.95.0) sit in a single contiguous region (file offsets 0x27153b–0x288051). The string constants that region references identify it as mimalloc (`mimalloc: `, `unable to free OS memory`, `corrupted thread-free list`). The crash function at 0x27c260 is mimalloc v2's `chacha_block()` from `libmimalloc-sys2-0.1.62/c_src/mimalloc/src/random.c` — ChaCha20 quarter rounds `mi_rotl32(x,16/12/8/7)` compile to `rorx $0x10/$0x14/$0x18/$0x19` with BMI2; the caller 0x27cb60 is `chacha_next32()`. The GDB crash address `0x...27c33c` is exactly the `rorx $0x10,%ecx,%ecx` inside `chacha_block`. The PRNG seeds mimalloc's heap cookies during `mi_random_init()` at first allocation, so it executes at startup — SIGILL on `--version` is expected on any CPU without BMI2 (pre-Haswell, e.g. the reporter's i7-3770). 2. **Nothing in the repo enables BMI2.** `.cargo/config.toml` has no `target-feature`/`target-cpu` flags for x86-64 Linux; no `#[target_feature]` in reachable workspace code (oxc_simd gates behind runtime detection); `rand`/`rand_chacha` are dev-dependencies only, and the Rust toolchain pin (`rustc 1.100.0`) is identical at both tags. `Cargo.lock` diff between `oxlint_v1.94.0` and `oxlint_v1.95.0` shows no dependency relevant to this (only oxc-internal version bumps); mimalloc-safe 0.1.66 / libmimalloc-sys2 0.1.62 and cc 1.2.65 are unchanged. 3. **The build path differs from the clean CLI.** In `.github/workflows/release_apps.yml` the same job builds both artifacts: the standalone CLI via `cross build` (runs inside Docker with the cross image's own, older GCC → both 1.94.0 and 1.95.0 CLI binaries contain zero BMI2 instructions — verified by disassembly of the GitHub-release binaries), while the napi binding runs `napi build --use-napi-cross` on the runner host. mimalloc is built through `cmake` (libmimalloc-sys2 build.rs) with the host `/usr/bin/cc` — no `-march` flag is passed anywhere (mimalloc v2's `MI_OPT_ARCH` only adds flags for arm64; x64 gets nothing). So mimalloc inherits the **compiler's default ISA**. 4. **The runner image's compiler changed between releases.** `.comment` sections of the shipped bindings: - 1.94.0: `GCC: (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1)` (Ubuntu 24.04 image; GCC default = baseline `x86-64`) → no BMI2. - 1.95.0: `GCC: (Ubuntu 15.2.0-16ubuntu1) 15.2.0` (Ubuntu 26.04 image), no other compiler present → mimalloc compiled by GCC 15.2. 5. **GCC 15.2 (Ubuntu 26.04) defaults to `-march=x86-64-v3`.** Verified on this triage runner, which has the identical `gcc (Ubuntu 15.2.0-16ubuntu1) 15.2.0`: - `gcc -Q --help=target` → `-march = x86-64-v3` - `printf 'unsigned rot(unsigned x){return (x<<16)|(x>>16);}' | gcc -O2 -S` → emits `rorx $16`; with explicit `-march=x86-64` → emits `rol`. - Compiling mimalloc's `random.c` with plain `gcc -O2` (no arch flags) yields **32 BMI2-family instructions** — the exact pattern and count found in the shipped 1.95.0 binary. Plain `clang -O2/-O3` yields zero. 6. **Local reproduction on the current checkout.** The repo's own prebuilt mimalloc artifacts (built on this machine with oxc's pinned toolchain, `target/release/build/libmimalloc-sys2-0fb1cad2772ce265/out/build`) show `CMAKE_C_COMPILER=/usr/bin/cc`, `CMAKE_C_FLAGS= -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -fPIC -m64 -w` (no `-march`), and its `random.c.o` contains the same 32 BMI2 instructions — i.e. the shipped-binary defect reproduces byte-pattern-for-pattern locally. 7. **The existing mitigation in newer `cc` is absent from oxc's pin.** Building the same mimalloc crate in a scratch project with the latest `cc 1.11.3` (vs oxc's pinned `cc 1.2.65`) makes cc-rs detect the v3 distro default and inject `-march=x86-64` itself: `CMAKE_C_FLAGS= ... -m64 -march=x86-64 -w` → **0** BMI2 instructions. So upgrading `cc` in `Cargo.lock` fixes the codegen even on the new image. ## Responsible components - Trigger: GitHub runner image change (`ubuntu-latest` → Ubuntu 26.04 / GCC 15.2 with distro default `-march=x86-64-v3`) — environmental, not a repo regression. - Root cause / defect location: - `Cargo.lock`: `cc 1.2.65` (too old to counteract the v3 compiler default with `-march=x86-64`). - `libmimalloc-sys2 0.1.62` build.rs (vendored `c_src/mimalloc`, built via `cmake` crate) — compiles C with the host `/usr/bin/cc` and no explicit baseline `-march` for x86-64 Linux. - `.github/workflows/release_apps.yml` `build-oxlint` job (x86_64-gnu matrix entry) — host-built napi binding is the only shipped artifact compiled by the runner's default GCC; its `TARGET_CC: clang` env ("# for mimalloc") no longer determines the compiler actually used by the cmake build (CMakeCache shows `/usr/bin/cc`). - Affected consumers: every prebuilt napi binding that enables the `allocator` feature and is built on the host: `@oxlint/binding-linux-x64-gnu` (this issue), plus the linux-gnu/musl x64 bindings of `oxc-parser`, `oxc-transform`, `oxc-transform-react`, `oxc-transform-relay`, `oxc-minify` (all depend on `mimalloc-safe`), and `oxfmt` if released via the same host path. Rust CLI binaries built through `cross` Docker images are unaffected. Non-x86 and macOS/Windows bindings unaffected. The i686-pc-windows and aarch64 entries don't use this host gcc path either. ## Minimal fix approach 1. Bump `cc` in `Cargo.lock` to a release that injects `-march=x86-64` when the C compiler's default exceeds baseline x86-64 (verified: cc 1.11.3 does; releases since the Ubuntu 26.04 v3-default change include it). This alone removes BMI2/AVX2 from mimalloc on the new runner image. 2. Defense in depth (either or both): - Pass an explicit baseline flag for x86-64 Linux targets — e.g. set `TARGET_CFLAGS: -march=x86-64` in the release workflow env for the linux-gnu/musl x64 matrix entries, or add `cmake_config.cflag ("-march=x86-64")` guarded to x86_64-linux in libmimalloc-sys2's build.rs (upstream fix for napi-rs/mimalloc-safe). - Pin `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` (or a toolchain container) for host-built napi jobs so the compiler default is stable. Verification for the fix: objdump the produced `*.node` and assert zero `rorx/shlx/shrx/andn/bzhi` (the count was 150 in the bad build, 0 in 1.94.0 and 0 in the locally rebuilt binding with cc 1.11.3). ## Supporting evidence files - `v1.95.0/disasm.txt`, `v1.94.0/disasm.txt` — full objdump of shipped bindings - `cli-1.94.0/`, `cli-1.95.0/` — GitHub-release CLI binaries (both BMI2-free) - Local rebuild artifacts: `target/release/build/libmimalloc-sys2/...` in the repo worktree (`random.c.o` with 32 BMI2 instructions, built with oxc's pinned `cc 1.2.65` on this GCC 15.2 image) and scratch projects `/tmp/mima_clang`, `/tmp/mima_gcc` (latest cc → `-march=x86-64` → 0 BMI2). ## Remaining uncertainty - Which exact `cc` release first added the `-march=x86-64` mitigation was not bisected; only that oxc's pin (1.2.65) lacks it and the current latest (1.11.3) has it. The precise GitHub runner image flip date is inferred from the two build dates and `.comment` evidence rather than an announcement. ## Confidence `high` — execution evidence identifies the specific defect: the identical BMI2 instruction sequence was reproduced byte-for-byte by rebuilding mimalloc's `random.c` on the same compiler image, the mechanism (GCC 15.2 distro default `-march=x86-64-v3`, no mitigation in pinned `cc`) is proven both positively (plain `gcc -O2` → rorx) and negatively (explicit `-march=x86-64`, or cc ≥ 1.11.3 → rol / 0 BMI2), and it explains every observed symptom (startup crash on `--version`, 1.94.0-vs-1.95.0 delta, clean CLI binaries, clean non-x64 and cross-built artifacts). --- # Verification — issue #30164 (verify stage) ## Reporter's claim `oxlint@1.95.0` (`@oxlint/binding-linux-x64-gnu@1.95.0`) SIGILLs at startup on a baseline x86-64 Linux CPU (Intel i7-3770, Ivy Bridge: SSE4.2+AVX, no BMI1/BMI2/AVX2), even on `oxlint --version`, while `oxlint@1.94.0` works on the same machine and Node.js. ## Applied contract The `linux-x64-gnu` binding is distributed on npm with `"cpu": ["x64"]`, `"os": ["linux"]` (verified in the shipped package's `package.json` and the repo's `npm/oxlint` template). This is the Node.js ecosystem's generic linux-x64 target: the native binding must load on any x86-64 Linux host that can run the supported Node.js versions (`^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`). Node.js itself runs on baseline x86-64 (the reporter's Node v22.23.3 runs fine), and the previous release `@oxlint/binding-linux-x64-gnu@1.94.0` is fully functional on the same CPU — establishing that the supported use case exceeded no documented or implicit capability limit.
